criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.

stories.notes: The synced plan.json has no requirements, guardrails, systems or measures, an empty project name, and placeholder dates (every release and due date on 2026-09-20). The page renders those as empty states rather than filling them in.

criteria.text: Given the system is ready for deployment, when the deployment process is initiated, then the system should be operational with core functionalities.
Given the system is deployed, when a core functionality is accessed, then it should perform as expected.
Trust: Given the deployment process, when it completes, then an audit log entry is created with deployment details.

stories.notes: Deploy with `npm run deploy` (on-premises, this machine). It opens the database, listens, checks /api/health and the asset records over HTTP with timeouts and capped retries, then writes a system.deploy audit event (version, commit, host, database, checks, duration); the deployment does not count until that event is written. Failures (port taken, health unreachable, database will not open, audit write fails) stop the server and are audited as system.deploy_failed where the database allows. Core functionalities agreed with the user: health check plus asset records (create/read, audited, idempotent by asset tag). Not done here: Active Directory sign-in and 2FA (REQ-010) — sign-in is still a development stand-in until STORY-012; near-real-time replication (REQ-002 option) is not built.

criteria.text: Given the system is connected to ESRI ArcGIS, when asset data is updated, then GIS layers should reflect these updates.
Given a GIS field value is changed, when I check the system, then it should show the updated value.
Trust: Ensure all GIS transactions are logged for audit.

stories.notes: Verified against a SIMULATED ArcGIS stand-in (tools/arcgis-standin, layer named 'SIMULATED · City Assets') that speaks the ESRI REST shapes the client uses: generateToken, layer metadata with editor tracking, query with paging, applyEdits, errors as HTTP 200 with codes 498/499. Not yet run against the City's real ArcGIS Enterprise 11.3: point ARCGIS_LAYER_URL / ARCGIS_TOKEN_URL / ARCGIS_USERNAME / ARCGIS_PASSWORD at it and run npm run gis-sync. Field ownership agreed with the user: the system owns ASSET_TAG, NAME, ASSET_TYPE, STATUS, LOCATION_DESC (pushed); GIS owns geometry and all other attributes (pulled, shown on the asset). A GIS edit to a system-owned field is audited as gis.mismatch and overwritten by the system value. Every GIS transaction is audited: gis.push, gis.push_failed, gis.pull, gis.mismatch, gis.sync_run, gis.sync_failed. Failure paths: auth (bad sign-in, rejected token, one refresh on expiry), latency (timeouts, capped retries; applyEdits never retried, adds look up the tag first so nothing duplicates), data mismatch (owned-field edits, unknown features, missing layer fields).

criteria.text: Given a Cityworks SQL export, when the migration runs, then permits, licenses, service requests, inspections, and work orders import with their GIS feature relationships intact.
Given attached documents up to ~200,000 files, when the migration completes, then each attachment is linked to its record and retrievable.
Given migrated data is designated read-only, when a user opens a historical case, then it is viewable for look-up and analysis and clearly marked read-only.
Trust the migration only when a reconciliation report shows source and target record counts match and zero orphaned GIS relationships remain.
